oneLiner: AMD is the only merchant vendor selling a complete CPU+GPU+networking AI rack as an alternative to Nvidia. The market is betting that the MI450/Helios ramp turns guided 2027 growth of more than 80% into durable earnings, and that warrants, margin dilution and thin cash flow do not eat the upside.

verdict.summary: Q3 2026 settled the execution question for now: Helios racks are live at five lead customers and management guided 2027 revenue growth above 80%. The October sell-off took the stock back to roughly what our probability-weighted case is worth, so the asymmetry is balanced rather than attractive: the base case only holds value, the bull case needs both a beat on 2027 and a mid-30s multiple, and the bear case (a 2027 that grows ~45% at lower margins) roughly halves it. Two things would move us to Positive: Q4 data center landing at the guided ~50% sequential step with gross margin holding 55%, and free cash flow recovering toward net income. A second quarter of sub-5% FCF margin with inventory still rising would move us to Cautious.
wtb: 2027 revenue lands near $94B (about +80% on ~$52B in 2026), with data center above 80% of sales.
Non-GAAP gross margin stays at or above ~54% while AI GPUs overtake server CPUs in the mix; each point is about $0.9B of 2027 gross profit.
Non-GAAP EPS reaches ~$16 in 2027 on ~1.72B diluted shares, i.e. warrant and M&A dilution stays near 4% rather than the full ~19% the OpenAI/Meta warrants allow.
Free cash flow recovers from 4% of Q3 2026 revenue to 15%+ by 2H 2027 as the ~$11.5B inventory build ships.

bear.why: HBM, packaging or rack-integration limits cap the 2027 ramp at ~+45%, PCs fall double digits and customers push back on HBM cost sharing, so non-GAAP net margin slips to ~24% (gross margin near 52%). With OpenAI financing in doubt the market treats AMD as a second-source cyclical and pays a low-20s multiple.

base.why: The guided >80% growth arrives (~$94B), data center is ~82% of sales and operating leverage lifts non-GAAP net margin to ~29% from ~26% in Q3 2026 despite a ~54-55% gross margin. Consensus 2027 EPS is ~$16, so the market pays ~30x trailing, about 21x the ~$23 2028 consensus, for a business still growing 40%+.

bull.why: Supply additions let 2027 double (~$104B): Anthropic's first GW, Meta and OpenAI deployments stack, agentic AI keeps server CPUs doubling, and gross margin holds 56% so net margin reaches ~31%. A visible 2028 step-up earns a mid-30s multiple on 2027 EPS.

scenarioModel.note: Non-GAAP EPS throughout (GAAP is distorted by non-cash warrant remeasurement, ~$1.1B in Q3 2026). 2026 revenue = Q1 $10.25B + Q2 $11.54B + Q3 $13.38B + Q4 guide ~$17.0B = ~$52.2B. EPS = revenue x non-GAAP net margin / 1.72B diluted shares (1.661B in Q3 2026 plus ~60M for partial warrant vesting and the World Labs stock deal): bear $76B x 24% = $18.2B / 1.72B = $10.60; base $94B x 29% = $27.3B / 1.72B = $15.85; bull $104B x 31% = $32.2B / 1.72B = $18.74. Multiples apply to 2027 EPS at end-2027. Siberforge estimates, not consensus.

debates.q: Does guided >80% 2027 growth arrive on schedule?
debates.bull: Helios racks are live at Anthropic, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI and Oracle; management says wafers, substrates, packaging and memory are secured for much higher 2027 growth, and Q4 is guided +27% sequentially.
debates.bear: Demand exceeds supply by management's own account, Helios is AMD's first rack-scale system, and Q4 already needs data center to rise ~50% q/q; one slipped quarter moves 2027 by billions.
debates.view: This sets the bear-vs-base gap ($10.60 vs $15.85 EPS). Q4 is the test: a clean ~50% data center step makes the 2027 framework credible; a miss moves weight to the bear case.

signpost.metric: Q4 2026 data center revenue vs Q3's $8.55B
signpost.threshold: $12.5B+ (about +46% q/q) confirms; below $11.5B is a miss

debates.q: How much of the profit is cash?
debates.bull: The Q3 cash dip is a deliberate ~$3B inventory build ahead of the Q4 ramp; trailing cash conversion through Q2 2026 was 157% and net cash was positive.
debates.bear: Q3 2026 free cash flow fell to $554M (4% of revenue) while debt more than doubled to $7.1B; net income ran at ~99% of operating income on a trailing basis, lifted by non-operating items and a large tax benefit that offset the warrant charge.
debates.view: Timing until proven otherwise, but this is the item that would move us to Cautious. We value on non-GAAP EPS, so cash has to catch up within two quarters.

signpost.metric: Free cash flow margin and inventory
signpost.threshold: FCF above 10% of revenue with inventory flat or down; a second sub-5% quarter is a red flag

debates.q: Is the price asking for more than AMD has ever delivered?
debates.bull: Revenue growth accelerated four quarters running (to +45% in Q3 2026, +66% guided for Q4), well above the 13.6%/yr three-year record; the 2027 guide is above the 35%+ long-term model.
debates.bear: The reverse DCF needs ~30%/yr FCF growth for a decade, and AMD pays for demand with warrants for up to 320M shares (OpenAI and Meta) plus equity stakes in customers (up to $5B in Anthropic, $1B in Meta).
debates.view: The multiple, not the growth, is the swing factor (22x vs 36x). We give it a base 30x only while warrant dilution stays modest and customer-funded demand does not grow faster than revenue.

signpost.threshold: above 1.75B before 2027 revenue doubles = dilution outrunning delivery

changelog.change: Migrated to v3 on the Q3 2026 print (Nov 3): beat ($13.4B, non-GAAP EPS $2.09), Q4 guide ~$17B, 2027 revenue growth guided above 80%. Added scenario values on 2027 non-GAAP EPS (bear $233 / base $476 / bull $675, weighted ~$465) and debates on ramp timing, cash conversion (Q3 FCF 4% of revenue) and dilution. View moved: from priced-for-perfection caution to Neutral, as fundamentals rose and the stock fell.

thesis: Data center now is the company. It reached 64% of Q3 2026 sales from 47% a year earlier, and management expects it to exceed 80% of 2027 revenue with AI GPUs overtaking server CPUs in Q4 2026.

Helios is past the prototype stage. Five lead customers brought racks online in Q3 2026 and OEMs (HPE, Dell, Lenovo, Super Micro) begin shipping systems in Q4, turning AMD from a chip supplier into a system vendor.
Agentic AI is a second engine. Server revenue is expected to roughly double in 2027 with Venice EPYC on 240+ platforms, a CPU tailwind Nvidia does not share.
Operating leverage is real. Non-GAAP EPS grew 74% on 45% revenue growth in Q3 2026, so even with a slightly lower gross margin, scale drives the base-case net margin from ~26% to ~29%.

latestProse: Q3 2026 (ended Sep 26; reported Nov 3) was a clean beat on the lines that matter and a weak one on cash. MI455X shipped in volume for the first time and Anthropic, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI and Oracle brought their first Helios racks online, with Venice EPYC launching on 240+ platforms. Client slowed sharply as memory-cost inflation hit late-quarter PC sell-through, and gaming fell on the console cycle. Cash went the other way from earnings: AMD built inventory for the Q4 ramp and issued debt, so free cash flow was the weakest in two years. Shares fell as much as 7.5% after hours, then traded flat the next day as analysts trimmed targets on sector multiples while raising 2027-2028 estimates.
guidanceProse: Q4 2026: revenue ~$17.0B plus or minus 3% (~+66% YoY, ~+27% q/q) at ~55% non-GAAP gross margin, with data center up ~50% sequentially and Client and Gaming down more than 20%. For 2027 management guided revenue growth above 80%, server revenue roughly doubling and data center above 80% of sales, while expecting PC units to fall double digits. No 2027 margin guide: AI systems dilute the corporate average and HBM cost inflation is being shared with customers. The CFO said warrant charges will rise as the OpenAI agreement progresses; they hit GAAP, not non-GAAP or cash.
segments: Data center: $8.55B in Q3 2026, 64% of revenue, +97% YoY (EPYC CPUs + Instinct MI450/Helios); guided ~+50% q/q in Q4.
Client and Gaming: $3.72B, -8% YoY (Client $2.9B +7%, Gaming $773M -40%); guided down 20%+ q/q in Q4.
competitive: Nvidia still dominates AI accelerator revenue and is already shipping Vera Rubin while Helios is just ramping; AMD's 2026 share is single-digit (exact figure unverified)
AMD claims a tokens-per-dollar advantage in large-scale inference and is expanding training capability with MI450 (Citi TMT, Sep 8, 2026)
Hyperscaler custom silicon (Google TPU, AWS Trainium, Broadcom ASICs) is a larger, faster-growing threat to merchant GPU vendors than AMD is to Nvidia
Versus Intel and Arm: agentic-AI CPU demand lifted all three in Sep 2026; AMD targets ~half of a $220B 2030 server CPU market across instruction sets
Cerebras partnership (Jul 23, 2026) pairs Helios throughput with wafer-scale low-latency decode, and the Taalas buy adds in-house ultra-low-latency inference silicon
moat: AMD's moat is chiplet design execution plus the only complete CPU+GPU+networking rack-scale alternative to Nvidia, reinforced by customers who strategically need a second source. ROCm software remains the soft flank versus CUDA, and the warrant-laced OpenAI structure shows AMD still pays for demand certainty rather than commanding it.
risks: Thin cash behind the earnings. Q3 2026 free cash flow was 4% of revenue against a ~26% non-GAAP net margin; if the inventory build does not convert in Q4-Q1, EPS is overstating the business.

Paying for demand. Warrants for up to 320M shares (~19% of shares) to OpenAI and Meta, an up-to-$5B equity commitment to Anthropic (Jul 22, 2026) and a $1B investment in Meta's equity offering (Oct 27, 2026) tie revenue to customer financing.

OpenAI is the weakest anchor. Reports in Oct 2026 put OpenAI's annualized revenue near $50B, about $20B below figures that had circulated (unverified), and a funding squeeze would hit the 6GW deal first.
Mix-driven margin dilution. Q4 gross margin is guided down to ~55% and HBM cost inflation is being shared with customers; the bear case assumes ~52%.
Supply and execution. Demand exceeds supply by management's account; a Helios or HBM slip lands in the quarters that carry the 2027 guide, while PCs are expected to fall double digits.

By end-2026: World Labs acquisition close (all stock), subject to regulatory approvals (debate 3).

~Early Feb 2027 (date unconfirmed): Q4 2026 report - data center step, gross margin, FCF and inventory (debates 1 and 2).
1H 2027: first gigawatt of Anthropic Helios deployment; OpenAI first-GW milestone and warrant vesting (debate 3).

valPresets.note: Year-1 FCF growth presets fade to terminal. The reverse DCF needs ~30%/yr FCF growth for 10 years versus 13.6%/yr revenue growth over the last three years; the base preset (35%) is roughly what guided 2027 growth implies if cash conversion recovers.
